To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CPG10101 is safe, well-tolerated, and induces a robust immune response.

CPG 101101, a novel unmethylated CpG oligodeoxynuclotide agonist of TLR9, was well tolerated in normal volunteers and induced interferons, chemokines and cytokines, including 2’5’-oligo adenylate synthetases, in a pattern consistent to the biology of TRL 9.

In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a new therapeutic strategy for the treatment of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection.
the development of a new class of drugs, the Toll-like Receptor-9 (TLR-9) agonists, which are designed to activate immune cells and stimulate the body’s own immune response to fight infection.
the development of a new class of immunostimulants that are based on the activation of the Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7) and 9 (TLRs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

CPG 1010101 (ACTILON™): (1) is well tolerated in healthy subjects, (2) induces a dose dependent pharmacodynamic effect, (3) has a favorable safety profile, (4) has an acceptable pharmacokinetic profile, and (5) is worthy of further clinical development.
CPG 101010 is safe, has an acceptable pharmacokinetic profile and is immunostimulatory, with the potential for clinical benefit.

CPG 1010 (ACTILON™ ) is a novel, potent and selective unmethyated cytidinephosphoguanosine oligodeoxynuclotide agonist of toll-like receptor 9, which is being developed for treatment of chronic infections including HCV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CPG10101 is a potent and selective unmethylation CPG containing oligodeoxynuclotides agonist of TLR9, and that it can induce interferons, cytokine and chemokines.
the TLR9 agonist CPG 101101 is safe, well tolerated and has a favorable pharmacokinetic profile.
the TLR9 agonist CPG 1010 was generally safe and well tolerated in normal volunteers and induced a robust immune response in a pattern consistent to the known biology of TLRs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune effects induced by CPG10101 were consistent with the expected biological effects of a TLR9 agonist, and that these effects were detectable at doses as low as 0.25mg.
the immune response induced by CPG 101101 can be monitored in the blood by a number of cytokines and chemotaxis factors.
the induction of IP-10 is a sensitive marker of CPG 9 activity.
